architecture.mechanism: Multi-grade thermal integration using staged high- and low-grade water-source heat pumps, coordinated by a dispatch strategy, to lift heat across multiple temperature grades and maximize primary energy savings through thermodynamic-economic multi-objective optimization.
architecture.intervention: Install a water-source heat pump (using an R-134a-replacement refrigerant such as R-513A or R-1234ze) in the 4.2 x 2.8 m plant room, coupled between the chiller condenser loop (~32 C) and the boiler feedwater preheat circuit, with a two-stage (low-grade lift from condenser loop to intermediate loop, high-grade lift to feedwater temperature) configuration and a load-following dispatch controller that prioritizes heat recovery whenever chillers and boiler demand coincide.
architecture.expected_effect: Recovery of a substantial fraction of the low-grade condenser heat currently rejected to cooling towers, raising it to feedwater preheat temperature, reducing boiler steam fuel consumption (targeting primary energy savings on the order of the paper's ~33% for the recovered stream), with projected payback under 6 years at $0.11/kWh and a 25-year service life for the heat pump hardware.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument the chiller condenser loop and boiler feedwater lines with flow and temperature sensors over a 4-week baseline period; then run the heat pump upgrade and measure (a) condenser heat diverted to cooling towers (should drop by the predicted recovered kW), (b) boiler fuel/steam input per ton of laundry and sterilization load (should decrease proportionally to recovered kWh), and (c) computed simple payback from metered energy savings at $0.11/kWh; if measured annual savings do not yield payback under 6 years or recovered heat is less than 50% of the design estimate, the mechanism transfer is falsified.
